newsitem.title: UK: Britain delays decision on new Eurofighter missile.
newsitem.headline: Britain delays decision on new Eurofighter missile.

text.p: The British government said on Monday that it has postponed for at least a year making a choice on bids to develop an air-to-air missile which it wants for the new Eurofighter aircraft.

Instead the Ministry of Defence (MOD) said that the two contenders would be paid 5.0 million pounds ($8.2 million) apiece to work for a year on reducing the development risks for the Beyond Visual Range Air-to-Air Missile (BVRAAM).
The two groups, led by British Aerospace Plc and U.S. group Raytheon Co's new acquisition Hughes, put in rival bids for the estimated 700 million pound project in June 1996.
Meteor is a multinational European grouping led by Matra BAe Dynamics, the joint venture between British Aerospace and Lagardere Group's Matra Defense.
"Further work is needed to reduce technical risk before a development and production contract can be let," the MOD said in a statement.
"This project definition and risk reduction phase will also give the bidders, Matra British Aerospace (UK) Ltd and Hughes (UK) Ltd, an opportunity to refine their bids."

British arms procurement minister John Spellar told parliament: "We have concluded that there is a need for further work to reduce risk in performance and timescale before we let a development and production contract."
He said subject to neogtiation it was intended to place the contracts for about 12 months' work with Matra BAe and Hughes in July and they would be worth five million pounds apiece.
"It is our intention to ensure that Eurofighter enters operational service with the most cost-effective equipment available," Spellar said.

The four-nation Eurofighter aircraft is being developed by British Aerospace, Daimler-Benz unit Daimler Aerospace, Finmeccanica's Alenia and Spain's Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (Casa). ($ = 0.610 British Pounds)
